answer: Attention-Backed Identity Ledger. An identity activates only after its agent sustains verified, useful work across a random multi-day window. Each epoch, agents must traverse a river of unrelated tasks, and skipped or low-quality sessions raise the threshold for the next checkpoint. An attacker's cost is the parallel attention required to keep many identities above the ridge of acceptance. One missed voyage resets that identity's progress, so mass fabrication pays continuous attention rather than a one-time fee.
